title: Rook endings: the Philidor defence
summary: The drawing method a pawn down: third rank, then check from behind.
body:
Defending rook and pawn against rook with your king in front of the pawn:

1. Keep your rook on your **third rank** (the 6th for Black). The enemy king can't advance in front of its pawn.
2. When the pawn steps onto that rank, the king has lost its shelter: drop your rook to the **back of the board** and **check from behind**.

Passive defence (rook on the back rank) usually loses; active defence draws.

examples.prompt: Black to move and draw. Where does your rook belong?
examples.explain: Ra6! - the rook on the third rank keeps the white king from reaching the 6th rank in front of its pawn.

examples.prompt: Black to move. The pawn advanced to e6 - switch plans.
examples.explain: Now the white king has no cover from checks: Ra1! and check from behind forever. Staying on the 6th rank loses.
Rf1+! The checks from behind start now; the white king can't escape them without leaving its pawn.
